title: ch says /ch/
parentNote: Two things start today. The sound is ch — a short sneeze of a sound, the noise a train makes, and like sh it belongs to both letters together rather than to either one. The error to listen for is a stretched-out /sh/ where the /ch/ should be, so "chip" comes out "ship"; say the two back to back and let them watch you — /sh/ pours out long and smooth, /ch/ stops dead the moment it starts. The second new thing is capital letters: from today every sentence begins with a big letter and names like Sam and Jack keep one. Big S and small s are the same letter wearing a different coat and they say exactly the same sound, so if your child stalls on a capital, write the small one beside it and they will almost always get it themselves.

activities.mouthCue: Tongue up behind your top teeth, then let it go in one quick puff — ch! It stops as soon as it starts.
activities.prompt: Another pair of letters sharing one sound. This one is short and sharp, like a little train.
One of these you can hold on forever. The other stops straight away. Find the one that stops.
All three are two letters with one sound. Listen for the little puff.
Three sounds. The c and the h hold hands, just like s and h did.
To chat is to talk to somebody. Keep the start quick.
Point at your chin while you say it.
Two letter teams and still only three sounds — ch at the front, ck at the back.
This time ch is at the end. It still stops the word dead.
A big S at the front. Big S and small s say the same sound — names get the big one.
Big J, small a, small ck. Only the first letter is wearing its big coat.
This is the one to get right. Does the start stop quickly, or go on and on?
One of these has the h doing its job. Listen to the very first sound.
Same start, same middle. The ending is the only clue.

activities.text: A chick can pick at a chip.
activities.prompt: The first letter is big now. That is how you know a sentence is starting.

activities.text: Jim will chat and Pam will chat back.
Did a chick nip at Kim?
activities.prompt: That hook at the end is a question mark. Let your voice go up.

activities.title: Sam and a chick
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Sam had a big chip in a sack.
A chick did dash in and pick at it.
Sam did grin at a chick.
A chick had a bit and Sam had a bit.

questions.prompt: Sam had a big chip in it.
It did dash in and pick at a chip.
